proposals.evidence: The complete predicate is thirst + be felt/strike. Turner explicitly lists Jaunsari tīś under *tṛṣyā and the neighbouring Jaunsari expression cīś lāgṇi to be thirsty; lagyati supplies lāg- be felt/begin. The final verbal endings are preserved as inflection; the two lexical constituents are recorded in order.

proposals.evidence: The full predicate is hunger + be felt/strike. Turner bubhukṣā lists Hindi bhūk(h), Old Marwari bhūkha, Oriya bhuk(h)a/bhoka and Jaunsari bhukh; lagyati supplies the matching regional lag-/lāg- paradigm, including Oriya lāgibā and western Pahari be felt. These responses contain two lexical constituents, with local tense/person/infinitive endings retained; clauses with additional copulas or progressive auxiliaries are excluded.
